title: Interior Grid Formats: News Publications
slide_intent: Show editors how to distinguish an independent picture story from a picture that belongs to an article. The grid and framing tell readers which words and pictures to read together.
strategic_value: NASA can use an underlying publication grid to accommodate short news items, longer articles and photo essays in one issue.
demonstration: Three sets of news spreads progress from two columns with a bracket around independent picture material to three-column examples with ruled photo essays and large pictures in looser groupings.
practical_value: Choose a two-column bracket for a self-contained image and caption, or a three-column scheme for a story that relies on several images.

content_islands.name: Editorial brief
content_islands.spec: Place the title at upper left and the guidance on article, photograph and caption relationships beside it. Key each example to its letter.

content_islands.name: News grid studies
content_islands.spec: Stack three rows of spread pairs at a common scale. Preserve the guides beneath text lines and image blocks. In b, align photographs to the top or bottom. In c, vary the scale and grouping of photographs.
